title: Logistics Network Manual
summary: Use supply tags, loadouts, manifests, and remote requests to make storage serve the route.

blocks.title: Overview
blocks.body: Logistics is the difference between owning materials and being able to use them. Its tools label supplies, bind routes, request loadouts, and reveal what the network can actually provide.

blocks.title: First Steps
blocks.body: Create a simple storage area, label categories, and bind one useful loadout before expanding. A first-aid route kit is often more valuable than a huge unsorted warehouse.

blocks.title: Core Loop
blocks.body: Tag storage, define loadouts, bind route manifests, scan readiness, and use remote requests when the network can fulfill the kit.

blocks.title: Important Systems
blocks.body: Supply Tags classify stock, Loadout Cards name expected kits, Route Manifests bind networks, and Remote Request Tablets scan or dispatch from a target block.

blocks.title: Integrations
blocks.body: PowerGrid keeps request blocks alive, Index and Wiki document items, Convoy benefits from staged cargo, and TutorialCore can explain missing network pieces.

blocks.title: Troubleshooting
blocks.body: If a request fails, check the bound target, network id, loadout id, stock rows, and whether the target block is still loaded and powered.
